title: After 2004, India built a tsunami warning centre
sources: INCOIS, Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre (incois.gov.in)
NCERT Class 11, ch. on natural hazards

quiz.q: India's Tsunami Early Warning Centre is run by:
quiz.why: Right. The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services, Hyderabad.

review.note: Written and voiced by Claude (AI voices, Kokoro), 8 Nov 2026. Not yet checked by a subject or Hindi editor. Check magnitude (9.1, USGS) and the centre's year (2007). Kept factual; no casualty figures.

lines.say: On the twenty-sixth of December 2004, a great earthquake struck off Sumatra.
Hours later, waves reached India's coasts with no warning.

beats.say: On the twenty-sixth of December 2004, a great earthquake struck off Sumatra. Hours later, waves reached India's coasts with no warning.

lines.say: one of the largest ever recorded.

beats.say: It was of magnitude 9.1, one of the largest ever recorded.

lines.say: A tsunami is a series of waves set off when the sea floor suddenly moves.
In deep water it's low and fast. Near the coast it piles up.

data.text: A series of waves caused when the sea floor suddenly moves.

beats.say: A tsunami is a series of waves set off when the sea floor suddenly moves. In deep water it's low and fast. Near the coast it piles up.

lines.say: In 2007, India set up its tsunami early warning centre at INCOIS, in Hyderabad.
It now serves the whole Indian Ocean region.
